Duration of spontaneous labour in ‘low-risk’ women with ‘normal’ perinatal outcomes: A systematic review - PMC
CG190 Intrapartum care for healthy women and babies: Full guideline 29/09/2023

reply.text: Childbirth length varies a lot. ACOG says labor usually lasts about 12–18 hours for a first baby and 8–10 hours for later births [1]. A review found the active first stage and pushing stage can be shorter, but the evidence was very uncertain and definitions varied [2]. NICE also notes wide normal ranges [3].

First and Second Stage Labor Management | ACOG
Duration of spontaneous labour in ‘low-risk’ women with ‘normal’ perinatal outcomes: A systematic review - PMC

reply.text: Usually, a second birth is shorter than a first. NICE’s evidence review found the full labour range for second or later babies was about 12.5–14.9 hours, but that is a range, not one exact usual time [1]. For the pushing stage, later births usually take less time than first births, but there is still wide variation [2][3].

sources.title: Assessment and support during early labour for improving birth outcomes | Cochrane

reply.text: Early labour in a first birth can vary a lot. Lamaze says it averages about 6–12 hours, but it can last 24 hours or more [2]. NICE defines the established first stage as starting at 4 cm and says first labours last about 8 hours on average and are unlikely to last over 18 hours [1]. So there isn’t one fixed length [3].
